title: Machine-learning analysis attributes the apparent pre-Norcia earthquake b-value rise to changing activity across two fault structures
summary: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values. Each structure retained its own b-value through the sequence; the apparent rise before the Mw 6.5 Norcia earthquake emerged when both were combined as their relative activity changed, showing that spatial heterogeneity can create an apparent temporal b-value signal.
ai_technology: Combination of machine-learning techniques for seismicity structure and b-value analysis (paper abstract does not name a single model)
organization: University of Naples Federico II; Scuola Superiore Meridionale

evidence.tested: For the 2016–2017 central Italy sequence, a combination of machine-learning techniques resolved two seismicity volumes with distinct fault orientations and Gutenberg–Richter b-values.
evidence.unknown: The analysis is retrospective and specific to the 2016/2017 central Italy sequence; the authors state that b-value changes may reflect spatial redistribution as well as other processes and do not claim a usable prospective earthquake precursor.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning analysis separated seismicity into fault-associated volumes and enabled comparison of their distinct b-values over time, supporting the reported explanation of the aggregate temporal change.
